question: The Dhakeshwari Temple in present day Bangladesh has been constructed under the rule of which dynasty?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sena**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Dhakeshwari Temple is one of the oldest and most revered Hindu temples in Bangladesh.
 
• It was constructed during the reign of the Sena dynasty, which ruled parts of Bengal from the late 11th century to the mid-13th century.
 
• The temple is dedicated to the Hindu Goddess Dhakeshwari, considered to be the guardian deity of Dhaka.
 
• The Sena dynasty was known for its patronage of art, culture, and religion, and they built several temples and monasteries during their rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sena Dynasty**

 
 
• The Sena dynasty was a Hindu dynasty that ruled Bengal after the Pala Empire.
 
• They are known for their contributions to literature, art, and architecture.
 
• Key rulers include Ballal Sena and Lakshman Sena.
 
 
 
• **Dhakeshwari Temple**
 
 
• It is located in Dhaka, the capital of Bangladesh.
 
• The name 'Dhakeshwari' means 'Goddess of Dhaka.'
 
• The temple is an important religious site for Hindus in Bangladesh.
 
 
 
• **Architectural Style**
 
 
• The temple showcases traditional Hindu architectural elements such as domes and spires.
 
• It has undergone several renovations over the centuries.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance**
 
 
• The temple is considered one of the Shakti Peethas, where parts of the Goddess Sati are believed to have fallen.
 
• It has been a center of cultural and religious activities in Dhaka for centuries.
